name: L7805CV
title: L78: 1.5 A fixed positive voltage regulators, 5 to 24 V
summary: Three-terminal linear regulators for fixed positive rails of 5, 6, 8, 8.5, 9, 12, 15, 18 or 24 V at up to 1.5 A, with thermal shutdown, current limiting and safe-area protection inside. C grades cover a 0 to 125 °C junction; A grades hold 2 % and come as AC (0 to 125 °C) and AB (-40 to 125 °C). Packages are TO-220 on two lead frames, TO-220FP, DPAK and D²PAK. L7805CV is the 5 V C-grade part in single-gauge TO-220.

circuits.title: DC parameter test circuit
circuits.description: The regulator with 0.33 µF from input to ground and 0.1 µF from output to ground: the setup for the DC figures.

circuits.title: Load regulation test circuit
circuits.description: A transistor switches the load resistor RL onto the output. Its base takes a 30 µs pulse from 0 V to VO through 100 Ω bypassed by 270 pF; the input carries 0.33 µF to ground.

circuits.title: Ripple rejection test circuit
circuits.description: The input is fed through 5.1 Ω, and a 120 Hz generator couples ripple onto the regulator side of that resistor through 470 µF. The regulator input has 0.33 µF to ground and the output drives an adjustable load RL.

circuits.title: Fixed output regulator
circuits.description: The basic rail: unregulated input on IN, the fixed output on OUT, 0.33 µF across the input and 0.1 µF across the output. The output capacitor helps the transient response and is not needed for stability; the input capacitor is needed when the regulator stands well away from the supply's filter capacitor.

parts.note: needed when far from the supply filter

circuits.title: Current regulator
circuits.description: R1 sits across OUT and GND, so the regulator holds VXX across it; the GND node becomes the output and feeds the load RL to ground. The load current is VXX / R1 plus the quiescent current Id.
notes: The input capacitor and the output capacitor both return to the GND pin node.

circuits.title: Circuit for increasing output voltage
circuits.description: A divider lifts the GND pin: R1 from OUT to the GND pin, R2 from the GND pin to ground. The output is VXX (1 + R2/R1) plus Id R2, with R1 carrying at least five times Id.

circuits.title: Adjustable output regulator (7 to 30 V)
circuits.description: An L7805 whose GND pin is driven by an LS141 wired as a follower. The follower copies the wiper of a 10 kΩ potentiometer across the output, so the output settles where the wiper voltage plus 5 V equals the output. The op amp runs from the input supply; 0.33 µF on the input, 0.1 µF on the output.

parts.note: op amp; pins IN+, IN-, OUT, V+, V-
potentiometer; pins 1 and 2 are the track ends, W the wiper

circuits.title: 0.5 to 10 V regulator
circuits.description: An L7805 on a split supply: its GND pin is driven by an LS141 that runs from +VI (13 to 25 V) and -VI (-7 to -17 V), so the GND pin can go below ground. R4 (910 Ω) and R5 (9.1 kΩ) from OUT to the GND pin feed the inverting input; the non-inverting input takes the wiper of a 10 kΩ potentiometer across the output, whose two parts are R1 and R2.

parts.note: op amp; pins IN+, IN-, OUT, V+, V-
potentiometer; pins 1 and 2 are the track ends, W the wiper; R1 is the part above the wiper, R2 the part below

circuits.title: High current voltage regulator
circuits.description: A BD536 PNP pass transistor carries current around the regulator. The regulator's input current flows through R1 (3 Ω) from VI; once the drop across R1 reaches Q1's VBE, Q1 conducts and supplies the extra load current straight into the output node. 0.33 µF on the regulator input, 0.1 µF on the output.

circuits.title: High output current with short circuit protection
circuits.description: The high-current circuit with a sense resistor RSC in Q1's emitter and a second PNP, Q2, across RSC to the base node. When the drop on RSC reaches Q2's VBE, Q2 turns on and starves Q1 of base drive, limiting the current to ISC = VBEQ2 / RSC. Q1 is a BD534, Q2 a 2N6124, R1 3 Ω.

circuits.title: Tracking voltage regulator
circuits.description: A positive L78 rail with a negative rail that follows it. Two 4.7 kΩ resistors in series run from +VO to -VO; an LS141 compares their midpoint with common and drives the base of a 2N6124 whose emitter is -VO and collector -VI. The op amp runs between +VI and -VI.

parts.note: op amp; pins IN+, IN-, OUT, V+, V-

notes: Misprint: a ground symbol is shown on the -VO node; -VO is a separate rail, not common.

circuits.title: Split power supply (±15 V, 1 A)
circuits.description: An L7815 and an L7915 share one ground to make ±15 V from ±20 V. 0.33 µF on the positive input, 0.1 µF on the positive output, 2.2 µF on the negative input and 1 µF on the negative output (both polarised, positive side on ground). A 1N4001 from ground to each output, reverse biased in normal running, guards against latch-up.

parts.note: negative regulator; pins IN, OUT, GND

circuits.title: Negative output voltage circuit
circuits.description: A positive regulator used for a negative rail. A transformer and bridge rectifier feed a floating supply; the regulator's OUT is the grounded output, and its GND pin together with the bridge's negative end is -VO. A polarised reservoir capacitor (no value given) sits across the bridge output and 0.1 µF across the regulated output.

parts.note: pins P1, P2 primary; S1, S2 secondary

circuits.title: Switching regulator
circuits.description: The L78 serves as the control element of a buck stage. A 2N3789 PNP switch from +VI drives a 1 mH inductor into the output, with a 1N5812 catch diode and 2000 µF on the output. The regulator's output is tied to VO; its input node feeds the switch base through Z1, and the switch base also has 4.7 Ω to +VI. 470 Ω from the switch node to the regulator's GND node and 0.5 Ω from that node to ground give the switching feedback; 10 µF on the input and 0.33 µF on the regulator input.

circuits.title: High input voltage circuit (configuration 1)
circuits.description: An NPN pre-regulator takes the excess input voltage. Its collector is on VI, and a zener from VI sets its base, with R from the base to the emitter; the emitter feeds the regulator at VIN = VI - (VZ + VBE). 0.33 µF on the regulator input, 0.1 µF on the output.

circuits.title: High input voltage circuit (configuration 2)
circuits.description: An NPN emitter follower ahead of the regulator: R from VI to the base, a zener VZ from the base to ground, collector on VI, emitter feeding IN. 0.33 µF on the regulator input, 0.1 µF on the output.

circuits.title: High input and output voltage
circuits.description: The configuration-2 pre-regulator with the whole regulator lifted by a zener VZ1 from its ground rail to ground, so VO = VXX + VZ1. The pre-regulator zener VZ2 returns to the lifted rail, and a diode D runs from that rail to VO, cathode on VO.

circuits.title: Reducing power dissipation with dropping resistor
circuits.description: A series resistor R between VI and the regulator input takes part of the drop and its heat. R = (VI(min) - VXX - VDROP(max)) / (IO(max) + Id(max)). 0.33 µF on the regulator input, 0.1 µF on the output, load RL.

circuits.title: Remote shutdown
circuits.description: A PNP switch Q1 in series with the input, turned on by Q2. A logic input drives Q2's base through R3; Q2 pulls Q1's base low through R2, and R1 from VI to Q1's base turns Q1 off when Q2 is off, removing the regulator's input. 0.33 µF on the regulator input, 0.1 µF on the output.

circuits.title: Power AM modulator (unity voltage gain, IO ≤ 0.5)
circuits.description: A modulation signal is coupled through a capacitor onto the GND pin, which returns to ground through 56 Ω. The output follows VXX plus the signal at unity gain. 0.33 µF on the input. It works well up to 100 kHz.

circuits.title: Adjustable output voltage with temperature compensation
circuits.description: A BC153 PNP (Q1) between the GND pin and ground sets the GND pin one VBE above its base. The base sits on a divider from VO: R1, then Q2 (a second BC153 wired as a diode, emitter to R1, base and collector together), then the rheostat R2 to ground. Q2's junction cancels the temperature drift of Q1's VBE; a polarised capacitor C from the base node to ground makes VO rise slowly. VO = VXX (1 + R2/R1) + VBE.

parts.note: potentiometer as rheostat; pins 1, 2 track ends, W wiper

circuits.title: Light controller, output falls as light rises
circuits.description: A PNP transistor from the GND pin to ground sets the GND pin one VBE above its base; the base hangs on a divider of a resistor from VO and, to ground, a photoresistor in parallel with a rheostat. More light lowers the photoresistor and the output. VO(min) = VXX + VBE.

parts.note: potentiometer as rheostat; pins 1, 2 track ends, W wiper

circuits.title: Light controller, output rises as light rises
circuits.description: The same PNP arrangement with the photoresistor moved to the top of the divider, from VO to the base, a rheostat from the base to ground and a polarised capacitor across the rheostat. More light raises the base and the output. VO(min) = VXX + VBE.

parts.note: potentiometer as rheostat; pins 1, 2 track ends, W wiper

circuits.title: Protection against input short-circuit with high capacitance loads
circuits.description: A diode from OUT back to IN, cathode on the input. If the input is shorted to ground (the switch) while a large output capacitor is charged, the capacitor discharges through the diode rather than through the regulator.

where.R1: resistor from OUT to the GND pin

equations.name: Raised output voltage
equations.expr: VO = VXX × (1 + R2 / R1) + Id × R2
equations.note: Condition on the divider: IR1 ≥ 5 × Id.

where.R1: upper part of the 10 kΩ potentiometer

where.VZ1: voltage of the zener under the ground rail

where.VBE: base-emitter voltage of the transistor under the GND pin

operation.text: L78 is a series of three-terminal positive linear regulators with fixed outputs of 5, 6, 8, 8.5, 9, 12, 15, 18 and 24 V, for local regulation on a board. Output current reaches 1.5 A, and above 1 A with enough heat sinking. With parts added round it, a fixed regulator also gives adjustable voltages or a regulated current. L7805CV is the 5 V commercial-grade part in TO-220 on the single-gauge frame.

C parts (L78xxC) have a 0 to 125 °C junction range. A parts hold the output to 2 %: AC over 0 to 125 °C and AB over -40 to 125 °C. Order-code endings: V for TO-220 on the single-gauge frame, V-DG for the dual-gauge frame, DT-TR for DPAK, D2T-TR for D²PAK and P for TO-220FP.

Three protections are inside the part: a current limit against short circuits, thermal shutdown when it dissipates too much, and safe-area compensation of the pass transistor, which lowers the short-circuit current as the input-output voltage rises. Output current and dissipation are therefore internally limited.

Low-current uses often run with no compensation capacitor at all. An input capacitor of at least 0.33 µF is wanted when long leads separate the regulator from the supply filter, or when the load capacitance is large; tantalum, mylar or another part that keeps a low impedance at high frequency suits, placed right at the input and ground pins with leads as short as possible, so the regulator stays stable at any load. The output capacitor is optional for stability and helps transient response.
There is no remote-sense pin, so ground loops and voltage drops along the leads must be kept small by careful construction.
The regulator needs a load of at least 5 mA to regulate.

Adding an operational amplifier lets the output be set higher than, or between, the fixed values while keeping the regulation figures. The lowest output this gives is 2 V above the regulator's own voltage.

operation.topic: Short-circuit protection of the high-current circuit
operation.text: The high-current circuit gains short-circuit protection from a sense resistor RSC and a second PNP transistor. That PNP must carry the regulator's own short-circuit current, so a 4 A plastic power transistor is named.
The modulator circuit, with the signal on the GND pin, works well up to 100 kHz at unity voltage gain and IO ≤ 0.5.
In the adjustable circuit with temperature compensation, Q2 is wired as a diode so its junction tracks the temperature change of Q1's VBE, and the capacitor C slows the rise of VO at start-up.

With a large load capacitance and an output above 6 V, an external diode from output to input protects the part when the input is shorted. The input then collapses fast while the output falls slowly, and the load capacitance discharges back through the base-emitter junction of the internal pass transistor; with enough stored energy that transistor fails. The diode carries this current around the IC to ground.
